semantic_changes: V4 is an authored semantic revision of router v3, not byte-equivalent to the original skill or a proven content-preserving compiler transformation.
Discovery frontmatter and both example references remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Only the two example references retain complete verbatim-source mappings.

The complete post-hook procedure and field templates now reside inside the numbered post-hook action checkpoint before final reporting, replacing the end-of-document procedure and pointer. The checkpoint requires the sent message itself to contain the selected blocks before automatic invocation; a promise to render them is insufficient. Both phases render at the left margin, without copying documentation indentation or code fences.

Reporting uses returned file bytes, completed messages and completed tool results as evidence. Missing metadata and untried tools do not establish unavailable capabilities; unsupported detail is omitted without adding exploratory commands solely to justify narration.
Questions about unspecified policies remain neutral about the eventual handling. A Gap marker cannot justify presupposing a restriction or other policy outcome.
Checklist discovery inventories the known-existing feature directory rather than directly listing a possibly absent checklist directory. Initial absence remains normal creation state.
V3 native-write and sandbox boundaries, pre-hook rules, constitution loading, per-topic allocation, Gap markers, exact append preservation and reviewer checkbox ownership remain in force.

validation_scope.offline: Package integrity, predecessor/source/discovery/example retention, routed-reference availability, retained-source mapping and tamper rejection. Checker/trace fixture tests are separate; no model instruction-compliance test is claimed.
validation_scope.fidelity_claim: Unvalidated candidate. Instruction changes and deterministic offline tests do not prove model compliance, semantic equivalence, sandbox behavior on a future host or runtime savings.
